title: Porsche China warns owners of fake vehicle-recall messages that could leak personal information, IT之家 reports
summary: IT之家 reports that Porsche China warned scammers are sending fake recall notices by text message and other channels to lure owners into clicking links and giving personal information. Porsche says these messages, files and links are not official and that its real recall notices never ask for bank card details, verification codes, transfers or payments. The warning says this could cause privacy leaks or financial loss.
plain: Porsche China says fake 'recall' messages are going around and may lead to leaked personal data or financial loss. It says its real recall notices never ask for bank card details, verification codes or payments.
exec: Porsche China says scammers are impersonating its recall notices, which could cost owners their personal data or money, as reported by IT之家.
action: Porsche China advises owners to treat such messages as unofficial, never give bank card details or verification codes, and to confirm any recall through the recall center website, Porsche China customer service or an authorized dealer.
geo_basis: country as the source states it (Porsche China statement); no city given
date_note: IT之家 gives only its publication day, 24 November, for Porsche's statement.

validation.note: Only IT之家 read; Porsche China's own statement was not read, so the warning is relayed by one publisher.

review.note: action advice: unknown calls/links/QR advice was SAMR guidance, not Porsche's; action now lists only Porsche's advice from IT之家
